newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 7.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.

- The UK Labour Party has ruled out early talks with Sinn Fein following Saturday's IRA disruption of the Grand National. Shadow Home Secretary Jack Straw said republicans had put themselves 'beyond the pale'.
- One of the State's main adoption agencies has admitted giving false information to adopted people about their parents.
- The number of people out of work is expected to fall again when the government announces live register figures later today.
- Coca Cola reports record sales of 465 million units in the Republic last year - an increase of 14 percent.
- Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring has ruled out a post-election deal with Fianna Fail.
- Up to 1,000 Irish racegoers will join English fans at Aintree today, defying the IRA, whose bomb hoaxes prevented the Grand National taking place there on Saturday.
- Market confidence in Ireland joining the single European currency leapt up last week in a league table compiled by investment bank JP Morgan.
